sceneFacts.shortVersion: The film's restaurant scenes were shot at The Langham, London.
sceneFacts.longDescription: The restaurant scenes in Burnt were filmed on location at The Langham, London, with the hotel's own restaurant, The Roux at The Landau, appearing throughout the movie. For authenticity, a fully functioning kitchen was built specifically for the film, designed to operate like a real professional kitchen. Michelin-starred chef and restaurateur Marcus Wareing served as the chef consultant, ensuring the culinary details were accurate.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Bradley Cooper based his chef character on three real chefs.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Bradley Cooper based his character, Adam Jones, on a combination of three celebrity chefs. He spent time with Marcus Wareing, Gordon Ramsay, and Marco Pierre White to research the role, incorporating their physical traits and characteristics into his performance. Consultant chef Marcus Wareing also helped teach the core actors, including Cooper, how to cook and act like chefs.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Actors learned to cook, preparing all food seen in the film for real.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Chef consultant Marcus Wareing was involved in every element of the food in the film, from kitchen design to recipe writing. To ensure authenticity, the actors learned how to cook, and all food preparation seen in the movie was done for real, without cooking doubles. Wareing worked closely with the core actors, including Bradley Cooper and Sienna Miller, to make them look believable as chefs.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: The film's kitchen realism earned a near-perfect score from a chef.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Michelin-starred chef Paul Liebrandt gave Bradley Cooper's portrayal in Burnt a near-perfect 9/10 accuracy score. Liebrandt specifically praised the film for its accurate depiction of the high standards and intense environment of a kitchen striving for Michelin stars. Cooper prepared for the role by training with renowned chefs, including Gordon Ramsay, to gain experience in a top kitchen. Consultant chef Marcus Wareing prepared all the recipes for the movie's fictional restaurant and ensured the kitchen set was fully functioning, making it work as a real kitchen.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Newspaper props are designed with legible details for authenticity.
sceneFacts.longDescription: The newspaper article seen here is an example of a graphic prop, meticulously designed to add real-world credibility to the film's setting. Many such props are not central "hero pieces" but are created as background dressing. Graphic designers ensure authenticity by using real, legible copy and carefully selected paper types, which enhances the experience for both the cast and the audience.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Alicia Vikander plays Adam's ex, Anne Marie.
sceneFacts.longDescription: Alicia Vikander plays Anne Marie, the ex-girlfriend of chef Adam Jones. Anne Marie is also the daughter of Adam's former mentor, the deceased master chef Jean-Luc. She and Adam shared a past of excess that led to their mutual downfall. Her character appears in only two scenes in the film.

sceneFacts.shortVersion: Actors cooked real food in a fully functioning kitchen.
sceneFacts.longDescription: The kitchen set for the film was a fully functioning environment, specially built for the movie. Consultant chef Marcus Wareing ensured that all food preparation scenes were done for real, with actors Bradley Cooper and Sienna Miller learning to cook and act like professional chefs. Miller, who worked the challenging fish station, became so proficient that she could have worked in a real kitchen. To enhance the realism, Wareing even turned the stoves on full to make the actors hot and sweaty.
